Frequently Asked Questions

Solvia Labs builds custom websites on Framer and Shopify with full client ownership and editing capabilities. The service model operates on a one-time project fee basis with no recurring agency retainers required after completion.


Clients receive full source files and admin access transfer upon project completion, retain complete ownership and editing rights over their website, and face no vendor lock-in or ongoing maintenance requirements to continue operating their site. This approach differs from traditional agencies that typically require monthly retainers for any changes or updates.

The ownership structure ensures clients receive full admin access to their website platform account, with all design files, assets, and source code transferred to the client upon project completion.


Websites are built without proprietary systems or Solvia Labs dependencies, allowing clients to maintain independent hosting and domain control. No recurring payments to Solvia Labs are required after project completion.


However, clients do pay ongoing costs directly to third parties, including domain registration, hosting fees, and third-party integrations like email services and payment processors. These costs are standard for any website ownership and are not paid to Solvia Labs.

Project timelines vary based on website complexity including page count, integrations, and custom features required, client content readiness such as copy, images, and brand assets, and the number of revision rounds and feedback cycles needed.


For estimated delivery, a landing page takes 7 days, a website with 3-5 pages typically take 20 business days, an online store or a website with 5-7 pages and integrations require 30 business days, e-commerce builds on Shopify need 21-28 business days, and custom requirements are evaluated case-by-case for timeline estimation.


The minimum delivery time is 7 business days from project kickoff to launch-ready website, representing the fastest possible turnaround for simple projects, without compromising on strategy or design.

Standard features in every project include responsive design optimized for mobile, tablet, and desktop viewing, SEO foundation setup with meta tags, Open Graph tags, and schema markup, Google Search Console integration and verification, Google Analytics 4 implementation with event tracking, and SSL certificate configuration for secure connections.


Framer-specific capabilities include CMS setup for dynamic content like blogs, portfolios, and case studies, animation and interaction implementation, custom breakpoint configuration for precise responsive control, and localization setup for multi-language sites.


Shopify-specific capabilities include product catalog setup and organization, payment gateway integration with Stripe, PayPal, and other processors, shipping zone configuration for multiple regions, discount and promotion system setup, and inventory management system configuration.

Solvia Labs specializes in two primary platforms: Framer for service businesses, SaaS companies, portfolios, and content-driven sites, and Shopify for e-commerce, physical product sales, and subscription businesses.


Platform selection criteria guide clients toward Framer for projects requiring no-code editing, visual design control, fast performance, and lower monthly costs, while Shopify is recommended for projects needing e-commerce functionality, payment processing, inventory management, and shipping integrations.


Solvia Labs does not support WordPress, Wix, or Squarespace due to platform limitations for client self-editing capabilities and performance optimization constraints.

Client training consists of a video walkthrough covering platform navigation and interface overview, content editing for text, images, and links, section management including how to add, remove, and duplicate components, page creation and navigation updates, CMS usage for blogs and portfolios, form submission management, and basic troubleshooting techniques.


Post-training support includes 7 days of email and chat support for technical questions and minor adjustments as clients become comfortable with their new platform.

Standard website projects exclude several services to maintain focus and timelines.


Brand identity design including logo, color palette, and typography system development is not included. Custom illustration or photography must be provided by clients or sourced separately. Video production is outside the project scope.


Ongoing content updates post-launch are the client's responsibility. Email marketing campaign setup beyond basic integration is excluded. Paid advertising campaign management is not provided.


Advanced custom coding beyond platform capabilities cannot be accommodated within standard projects. Clients may reach out to Solvia labs for optional add-on services like content strategy consultation, professional copywriting, or one-off technical support.

Phase 1 is Discovery, which includes a strategy session covering business goals, target audience, and competitor analysis, a content audit of existing materials and messaging framework, technical requirements gathering for integrations and functionality specifications, and sitemap and wireframe approval.


Phase 2 is Design and Development, involving visual design in Framer or Shopify, client review and revision cycles with 2 free rounds included, content integration into the designed layouts, and functionality implementation and testing.


Phase 3 is Launch, consisting of final review and quality assurance, SEO configuration and verification, analytics setup and testing, domain connection and SSL configuration, a training session, and official launch.


For 7 business days after Launch, we provide bug fixes and technical troubleshooting, minor content adjustments, and responses to platform usage questions.

Pricing follows a fixed-price project quote model based on scope, with several factors determining the final cost. These factors include page count and complexity of each page, custom functionality requirements, integration needs with systems like CRM, email platforms, and payment processors, content volume and migration requirements from existing sites, and timeline urgency for expedited delivery.


Payment structure includes a 50% deposit and 50% on completion. Client may alsoo opt for more flexible terms. The value proposition compares a one-time payment to ongoing agency retainers, which typically cost $500-1,000 per month in the market, totaling $6,000-12,000 annually for services clients can eventually perform themselves.

Migration services are available and include content migration from old platforms to Framer or Shopify, URL structure preservation with 301 redirect mapping to maintain SEO rankings, and design modernization while retaining brand consistency.


Common migration scenarios include escaping agency lock-in situations where clients want ownership, moving from outdated platforms like WordPress or Wix, Shopify store redesigns for improved performance, and transitions from custom-built sites to no-code platforms.


Migration timelines typically add 5-7 days to standard project timelines depending on content volume and complexity of the existing site structure.

After the 7-day support period, clients have several post-support options. Most commonly, websites are self-managed, with clients handling all updates independently using the skills learned during training. For specific technical needs, on-demand support is available at an hourly rate for assistance.


Monthly retainers provide an ongoing support package for clients who prefer continuous assistance, though this is optional and not required to maintain the website. Client capabilities after handoff include full editing and content management access, the ability to hire independent contractors or in-house team members to make changes, and zero dependency on Solvia Labs for site operation or basic updates.
